fixes.explanation: That's the one! Moses asks the officers, "Have you spared all the women?" (Numbers 31:15) He's angry when he asks it, and the very next verse is where he explains himself. I think this is a heavy part of the story, and it's worth reading slowly.

Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, is a name tied to Balaam, so I get why it came to mind. Numbers 22:4–5 says Balak was king of Moab and that he sent messengers to Balaam. But Moses doesn't name him here. He says it was "…through the counsel of Balaam…" (Numbers 31:16) So the answer is Balaam son of Beor.

Og king of Bashan is a king Israel fought and defeated earlier (Numbers 21:33–35), but he isn't in this verse. Moses says the women caused it "…through the counsel of Balaam…" (Numbers 31:16) So the answer is Balaam son of Beor. Og can sit this one out.
